::: {#rem-scheme-racket}
#### Scheme and Racket

Stanford's CS 107, *Programming Paradigms*, taught Scheme in its Spring 2008 offering,
and its lectures are free to watch [@cain2008cs107videos].
Racket grew out of Scheme,
and most of the Scheme code in those lectures runs in Racket with few changes:

- Scheme's `car` and `cdr` return the first element of a list and the list of the other elements.
  Racket accepts them too,
  but this course uses their clearer names `first` and `rest`.
- A Scheme file needs no first line.
  A Racket file starts with `#lang racket`.
- Racket writes the cases of a `cond` in square brackets, `[test a]`,
  where Scheme uses parentheses.
  Racket accepts both.
- CS 107 typed its code into an interpreter called Kawa.
  This course uses DrRacket.

*Video:* Jerry Cain introduces Scheme, its lists and its first recursive functions in [CS 107 Lecture 19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_cV8NWQCxnE) [@cain2008cs107videos].

:::
